dedupe_keys.name: corn soy data layer csdl 30 m corn and soybean maps of the us midwest 1999 2018

description: The Corn-Soy Data Layer maps corn, soybean and other crops at 30 m across the US Midwest for every year from 1999 to 2018, filling gaps before the NASS Cropland Data Layer covered the region well. The Zenodo record says a random forest in Google Earth Engine was trained on Cropland Data Layer labels from 2008 to 2018 using harmonic regression features of Landsat 5, 7 and 8 surface reflectance, and validated against earlier Cropland Data Layers, county crop acreage and state crop rotation statistics. It was first published on 7 April 2020 by Sherrie Wang, Stefania Di Tommaso, Jillian Deines and David Lobell, with later versions to March 2021, as one GeoTIFF per year of about 190 MB, downloadable and free under CC BY 4.0, and also hosted on Google Earth Engine. Coverage is the Midwest states. Caveats: only corn and soybean are separated, and accuracy is lower in early years with fewer Landsat images. For simulation it gives field-scale crop history for drought and flood exposure of the corn belt, and for crop water, drainage and grain transport models. Related catalogue records include the USDA NASS Cropland Data Layer and the USGS modeled crop cover 2000-2013.
